body.statement: For every rational \(0<\eta<3/20\), \(P^{\diamond}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), \(\psi^{\diamond},\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\in\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), and \(F(\psi^{\diamond})=F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}})=P^{\diamond}\). The global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and have exactly two classes. Their ATT vectors are \((9/250,-33/2500)\) and \((-1/500,49/5000)\), so \(\mathcal I_{0,3}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-1/500,9/250\}\) and \(\mathcal I_{0,4}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-33/2500,49/5000\}\). Moreover, \(\mathcal C_\eta^{\diamond}\) is a nonempty relatively open sign chamber in the named collision variety; every law in a relative neighborhood of \(P^{\diamond}\) within that chamber has two separated quotient ATT components with the same branch labels and coordinatewise ordering.
body.justification: A rational witness and a relatively open singular chamber show that disconnected geometry is structural rather than a numerical artifact at one isolated law.
body.gap: Generic label-switching observations do not establish a causal ATT gap after quotienting simultaneous labels, and the cited mixture papers provide no one-collision open chamber with exact values.
body.consumer: Regression tests for \(ak\) can verify exact branch retention and prevent software from replacing two attainable values by their interval hull.
body.proof_tex:
First compute the arm probabilities of \(\psi^{\diamond}\):
\[
 p_1=\tfrac12\tfrac35+\tfrac12\tfrac25=\tfrac12,
 \qquad p_0=\tfrac12.
\]
The control posterior weights are \((2/5,3/5)\), and the treated posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\).  For \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), the type probabilities are \((3/5,2/5)\) and both propensities are \(1/2\); hence its posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\) in both arms.  Its treated components are unchanged, while its control component of weight \(3/5\) is the former second component and its component of weight \(2/5\) is the former first component.  Commutativity of a two-term mixture therefore gives, for all \(i,j,k,l,d\),
\[
 F(\psi^{\diamond})_{ijkld}
 =F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}})_{ijkld}=P^{\diamond}_{ijkld}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Every displayed primitive lies in \([1/5,4/5]\subset[\eta,U]\), because \(0<\eta<3/20\).  In both representations the control terminal probabilities after state \(0\) equal \(1/2\), while the three noncollided differences are
\[
 \tfrac{7}{10}-\tfrac25=\tfrac3{10},\qquad
 \tfrac15-\tfrac45=-\tfrac35,\qquad
 \tfrac7{10}-\tfrac3{10}=\tfrac25,
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus the collision index is exactly \(k_0=0\).  We now prove that (15) exhausts the global fiber.

For one arm define the observable \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrices
\[
 Q_{jk}(l,i)=\mathbb P(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
\]
Any two-type representation factors them as
\[
 Q_{jk}=V_k\operatorname{diag}(g_{1j}(k),g_{2j}(k))S_j,
\]
where the columns of \(V_k\) are \((1-v_{zk},v_{zk})^\top\), \(g_{zj}(1)=\kappa_{zd3j}\), \(g_{zj}(0)=1-\kappa_{zd3j}\), and
\[
 S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j).
\]
In the treated benchmark, both \(V_0,V_1\) are invertible.  Also
\[
 \det S_j=w_{11}w_{21}B(a_{10};j)B(a_{11};j)(u_{21}-u_{11})\ne0,
\]
because the two types have the same pre-transition row and \(u_{21}=3/5\ne2/5=u_{11}\).  Thus all four \(Q_{jk}\) are observably invertible.  The observable product
\[
 Q_{01}Q_{00}^{-1}Q_{10}Q_{11}^{-1}
 =V_1\operatorname{diag}\left(
 \frac{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{1130})}{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{1131})},
 \frac{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{2130})}{\operatorname{odds}(\kappa_{2131})}
 \right)V_1^{-1}
\]
has the two distinct eigenvalues
\[
 \frac9{49}\quad\text{and}\quad 6.
\]
Therefore its two one-dimensional eigenspaces determine the probability columns of \(V_1\), after normalizing each column to sum to one, up to permutation.  Next, column normalization of
\[
 Q_{00}Q_{01}^{-1}V_1
 =V_0\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{1-\kappa_{1130}}{\kappa_{1130}},
 \frac{1-\kappa_{2130}}{\kappa_{2130}}\right)
\]
recovers \(V_0\) in the same order.  Finally,
\[
 S_j=V_0^{-1}Q_{j0}+V_1^{-1}Q_{j1}
\]
recovers \(S_j\); row sums of its two summands recover \(\kappa_{zd3j}\), and summing \(S_0+S_1\) recovers \(w_{zd},u_{zd},a_{zi}\).  Hence every treated-arm decomposition is the displayed one up to a type permutation.  In particular, every globally compatible representation has
\[
 a_{10}=a_{20}=\tfrac3{10},\qquad
 a_{11}=a_{21}=\tfrac45.
 \tag{17}
\]

It remains to identify the control decomposition under (17).  Write
\[
 g_{ij}=\mathbb P(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
\]
\[
 h_{ij}=\mathbb P(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
\]
Exact summation of the cells in (15) gives, with rows indexed by \(i\) and columns by \(j\),
\[
 (g_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}41/115&111/230\\[2pt]23/45&11/30\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 (h_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}103/575&174/575\\[2pt]49/225&14/75\end{pmatrix},
 \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb P(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\tfrac12
 \tag{19}
\]
for every \(i,j\).  Let \(\lambda_i=\mathbb P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0)\), let \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{z0,3,j}\), and let \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{z0,4,k}\) in an arbitrary compatible decomposition.  Equation (17) makes \(Z\) conditionally independent of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,D=0)\), so
\[
 g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The two row differences in (18) are \(-32/207\) and \(8/69\), both nonzero.  Thus \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\) and \(q_{1j}\ne q_{2j}\) for both \(j\).  From (19),
\[
 \lambda_i(1-q_{1j})(v_{10}-\tfrac12)
 +(1-\lambda_i)(1-q_{2j})(v_{20}-\tfrac12)=0,
 \qquad i=0,1.
\]
The determinant of these two equations in the two terminal deviations is
\[
 (\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(1-q_{1j})(1-q_{2j})\ne0,
\]
because the box makes \(q_{zj}<1\).  Hence
\[
 v_{10}=v_{20}=\tfrac12.
 \tag{21}
\]

For \(k=1\), equations (18) and (20) give the observable slopes and intercepts
\[
 \beta_j=\frac{h_{0j}-h_{1j}}{g_{0j}-g_{1j}},
 \qquad (\beta_0,\beta_1)=(\tfrac14,1),
\]
\[
 h_{ij}-\beta_jg_{ij}=c_j,
 \qquad (c_0,c_1)=(\tfrac9{100},-\tfrac9{50}).
 \tag{22}
\]
Since the two \(\lambda_i\)'s are distinct, equality of the two affine mixtures in (22) forces, separately for \(z=1,2\),
\[
 q_{z0}(v_{z1}-\tfrac14)=\tfrac9{100},
 \qquad q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\tfrac9{50}.
 \tag{23}
\]
The observed identity \(g_{i1}=\tfrac34(1-g_{i0})\) holds for both rows of (18).  Applying the same two-point affine-mixture argument to (20) yields
\[
 q_{z1}=\tfrac34(1-q_{z0}),\qquad z=1,2.
 \tag{24}
\]
Writing \(x=q_{z0}\) and \(v=v_{z1}\), equations (23)--(24) reduce to
\[
 x(v-\tfrac14)=\tfrac9{100},qquad
 (1-x)(1-v)=\tfrac6{25}.
\]
The first equality has \(v\ne1/4\), and substitution of \(x=9/(100v-25)\) into the second gives
\[
 (100v-34)(1-v)=24v-6,
\]
or
\[
 50v^2-55v+14=(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
 \tag{25}
\]
Thus the unordered control component pairs are exactly
\[
 (q_{z0},q_{z1},v_{z1})=(\tfrac35,\tfrac3{10},\tfrac25)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (\tfrac15,\tfrac35,\tfrac7{10}).
 \tag{26}
\]
Using (20), the latter component has \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=(14/23,2/9)\).  Since \(\mathbb P(X_1=0\mid D=0)=23/50\), this gives
\[
 w_{10}=\tfrac{23}{50}\tfrac{14}{23}+\tfrac{27}{50}\tfrac29=\tfrac25,
 \qquad
 u_{10}=\frac{(27/50)(2/9)}{2/5}=\tfrac3{10},
\]
and the other component has weight \(3/5\) and initial probability \(7/10\).  Equations (17), (21), and (26) therefore recover exactly the displayed control arm up to permutation.

Both arms are now unique up to their separate labels.  Their two relative alignments are feasible: the displayed alignment gives \((\pi,e_1,e_2)=(1/2,3/5,2/5)\), while the crossed alignment gives \((\pi,e_1,e_2)=(3/5,1/2,1/2)\).  All values have strict box slack.  There are no other global representations.  Equations (16) and (21) also show that every representation lies in \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\); hence \(P^{\diamond}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the global and stratum fibers coincide, and quotienting simultaneous labels leaves exactly two classes.

For the first alignment, the treated-type untreated recursions give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=(\tfrac12,\tfrac25,\tfrac{29}{50}),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=(\tfrac35,\tfrac{21}{50},\tfrac{229}{500}).
\]
The observed treated means are
\[
 (O_3,O_4)=(\tfrac{111}{250},\tfrac{259}{500}).
\]
Weighting the untreated means by \((3/5,2/5)\) gives
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond};P^{\diamond})
 =(\tfrac9{250},-\tfrac{33}{2500}).
\]
For the crossed alignment, the corresponding weighted untreated means are \((223/500,2541/5000)\), so
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}};P^{\diamond})
 =(-\tfrac1{500},\tfrac{49}{5000}).
\]
The two-class exhaustion proves the two displayed marginal sharp sets; no interval between their points is attainable.

Finally, let \(Z_\eta\) be the common zero set of those members of \(\mathscr L_{0,\mathrm{id}}\cup\mathscr L_{0,\mathrm{sw}}\) that vanish at \((P^{\diamond},\eta)\).  By definition,
\[
 \mathcal C_\eta^{\diamond}
 =Z_\eta\cap\bigcap_{g(P^{\diamond},\eta)>0}\{g>0\}
 \cap\bigcap_{g(P^{\diamond},\eta)<0}\{g<0\}.
\]
It contains \(P^{\diamond}\) and is relatively open in \(Z_\eta\), whose defining equalities include the three collision minors.  By cylindrical lifting in the cited cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition lemma, after shrinking to the relative CAD cell containing \(P^{\diamond}\), the accepted root sections are continuous semialgebraic functions and their branch and Thom labels are constant.  The exact fiber calculation above leaves two quotient sections.  Their coordinate gaps at the benchmark are \(19/500\) and \(23/1000\), both positive.  Continuity therefore supplies a relative neighborhood in which the same two labeled components remain separated and preserve the respective coordinatewise orderings.  This proves the chamber assertion, including its singular support qualification.
